provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. GlobalBandJets is the paper's S_α with the same two encoding choices as (6.24): iterated Fréchet jets of order j ≤ m in place of the coordinate multi-index ∂^I_{Z,T} with I ∈ ℕ₀², and one constant pair (C, p) per order m in place of per-multi-index C_{j,I}, b_{j,I} (equivalent because only finitely many I have |I| ≤ m; take maxima, and S_* ≥ 1 makes raising the exponent harmless). No ζ or δ factor appears, matching the paper: S_α is the unweighted slow class. The second encoding, UnweightedClass over slowStripData, is literally the same bound, since slowStripData sets delta ≡ 1 and zeta ≡ 1 so majorant collapses to C · ε^α · S^p. The repository states the agreement of the two encodings as two separate one-way lemmas rather than as one iff: globalBandJets_unweighted (MeanMomentBounds.lean:114) takes GlobalBandJets plus a smoothness hypothesis (hf : ∀ n, ContDiff ℝ ∞ (f n)) to UnweightedClass, and slowClass_globalBandJets (StateMomentBalances.lean:1021) takes UnweightedClass back to GlobalBandJets with no smoothness hypothesis; the smoothness asymmetry is because UnweightedClass carries a smoothness field that GlobalBandJets does not. The underlying space is the slow pair (Z,T) in both.
